meta.note: A snapshot of the Pokémon TCG card-image ecosystem. Links marked verified are pixel matches; the rest are the sites' own statements or indirect evidence. Not legal advice.

official.label: Official Pokémon
official.desc: The Pokémon Company, its regional companies and its game clients. The only true origin of digital card images.

extract.label: Game-client extract
extract.desc: Renders pulled out of the official game clients and re-published.

dataset.label: Scraped dataset
dataset.desc: A dump of an official source, published as a dataset.

rehost.label: Fan database / API
rehost.desc: Card databases and APIs. Mostly re-host digital images from upstream sources.

wiki.label: Fan wiki
wiki.desc: Community wikis. Modern cards re-hosted, vintage cards uploaded by users.

scan.label: Scan / photo source
scan.desc: Images made by scanning or photographing physical cards. Owned by whoever scanned them.

market.label: Marketplace / tracker
market.desc: Shops, price guides and collection trackers.

tcgdex.label: TCGdex
tcgdex.desc: The open card database this atlas centres on.

print.label: Printed cards
print.desc: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo.

sources.name: Printed cards

terms.summary: Every card is © The Pokémon Company / Nintendo / Creatures / GAME FREAK (Wizards of the Coast for the 1999–2003 English prints). A scan or photo adds the scanner's own rights on top.

sources.origin: For Western cards from Base Set to Platinum (1999–2010), and for Japanese cards before 2006, TPC never published a digital image online. Every picture of those cards anywhere, TCGdex's included, is somebody's scan or photo.

sources.name: Pokémon TCG Online (game client)
sources.eras: HGSS (2010) → Sword & Shield (2023), plus promos and trainer kits

terms.summary: Covered by the pokemon.com Terms of Use, which forbid reverse-engineering any part of any Service. Retired in 2023.

sources.origin: TPC's own digital card renders, shipped inside the game client.

sources.name: Pokémon TCG Live (game client)
sources.eras: Scarlet & Violet (2023) → Mega Evolution, plus promos

terms.summary: pokemon.com Terms of Use: no reverse-engineering, no bots or scripts.

sources.origin: TPC's own digital card renders, shipped inside the game client.

sources.name: pokemon-card.com (Japan)

terms.summary: Personal enjoyment only. No copying, reproducing, distributing or putting the images on the internet.

sources.origin: The Pokémon Company's official Japanese card database. Stops at the last regular number: SM/early-SwSh secret-rare tails and M6a 104–135 are not listed. Nothing before DP (2006).

sources.name: asia.pokemon-card.com (tw · th · id · sg · hk)
sources.eras: zh-tw S4 (2020) → today · th/id S5 (2021) → today · sg English print

terms.summary: Use only inside the site. No copying, distributing, or reproducing works to create links.

sources.origin: The Pokémon Company's official Asian card databases. The Singapore site carries the international English print at 744×1040, larger than TCGdex's 600×825 English images.

sources.name: pokemon.com card database

terms.summary: Personal, non-commercial use. No bulk download into a database, no bots or scripts.

sources.origin: TPC International's official Western card search. Useful only as a witness: the images are too small.

sources.name: pokemoncard.co.kr (Pokémon Korea)

terms.summary: No reproduction or distribution without the company's consent, except where the law allows.

sources.origin: The only official Korean source. The image CDN serves only a watermarked directory (data/wmimages/…); every other path is refused.

sources.name: Pokémon Shanghai WeChat mini-program

terms.summary: Official Simplified Chinese card database, reachable only inside the WeChat app.

sources.origin: The only official source of Simplified Chinese card images anywhere. pokemon.cn itself shows product art only.

sources.name: malie.io

api.note: JSON exports + open CDN (PTCGO archive and TCG Live export)

terms.summary: No licence. Asks for a credit, "not a legal or licensing requirement". The images come from game clients whose terms forbid reverse-engineering.

sources.origin: Extracted from the Pokémon TCG Online and TCG Live game clients. The de-facto origin of nearly every clean Western digital card image from HGSS onward: TCGdex, pokemontcg.io, pkmncards, TCGplayer, TCG Collector and the wikis all carry its files.

sources.name: duanxr/PTCG-CHS-Datasets (GitHub)

api.note: images + ptcg_chs_infos.json in a Git repo

terms.summary: Non-commercial or research use only. No redistribution without explicit written consent from Pokémon Shanghai.

sources.origin: A scrape of the official Pokémon Shanghai WeChat mini-program, at the app's native 300×419. The only Simplified Chinese image set outside the app.

sources.name: Pokémon Paradijs scans ("Martin")

terms.summary: The scanner's own work; no licence published. pkmncards.com credits "Martin of Pokémon Paradijs" for most of its pre-HGSS images.

sources.origin: One person's high-quality scans of English vintage cards. The most copied scan set on the web: pkmncards, pokemontcg.io, Scrydex, TCGdex, TCGplayer and TCG Collector all serve the same files.

examples.label: Base Set Charizard, as served by pokemontcg.io

stats.label: on TCGdex
stats.value: 15.5% of all en+de images, 98–99% of English 1999–2010

sources.name: bisafans.de

submissions.how: E-mail scans of cards they are missing to tcg@bisafans.de

terms.summary: All rights reserved, no reuse licence. Under German law even a plain scan or photo is protected (§72 UrhG).

sources.origin: Its community's own scans (600-dpi flatbed) and phone photos (EXIF: Galaxy S10, iPhone 11 Pro, Huawei). BW sets carry a "Bisafans.de" watermark. A few recent promos are official press images. Not re-used by any other site we checked.

sources.name: pkmcards.fr

terms.summary: No terms, legal notice or licence published at all, so nothing is granted.

sources.origin: Everything re-encoded to 400 px WebP. Modern cards are malie renders; French vintage (DP era and older) matches no official source, so scans of unknown origin. Many of those files are identical to TCGdex's French vintage images.

examples.label: Aquapolis H1 (French vintage, no official match)

sources.name: yuyu-tei.jp (shop)

terms.summary: The shop owns its images: "如何なる場合であっても無断での転載を禁止" (no reposting without permission, in any case).

sources.origin: The shop's own scans of its stock. 80% match no official file at all; the tile test identifies them as scans even where they look digital.

sources.name: pokeca.net

terms.summary: Third-party shop images, watermarked with the site's address.

sources.origin: Japanese shop images. Bulbagarden's Japanese secret-rare files are credited "From Pokeca.net" and carry its watermark.

sources.name: Pokécardex

terms.summary: Member scans. In 2016 its moderators declined to share unwatermarked copies and said they had no authority to distribute members' work.

sources.origin: About 23,000 Western and 24,000 Japanese scans by its members, all watermarked.

sources.name: pkmncards.com

terms.summary: No licence. Says the images are © TPC et al.

sources.origin: Credits "Martin of Pokémon Paradijs" for most pre-HGSS images, and nago/malie.io (PTCGO, TCG Live) from HGSS on.

sources.name: pokemontcg.io

api.note: Free API, announced to go offline on 2027-03-01 (successor: Scrydex). Data repo on GitHub.

submissions.how: Pull requests to the data repo

terms.summary: No licence at all, the data repo included. Developer terms cover accounts only.

sources.origin: HGSS → today: malie's renders. Base Set → Platinum: the Pokémon Paradijs scans. English subsets TCGdex lacks (Shiny Vault, Trainer/Galarian Gallery, promos) are malie renders too; better taken from malie directly. EX trainer kits and McDonald's are scans of unclear origin.

sources.name: Scrydex

terms.summary: Commercial service; see its terms.

sources.origin: Identical to pokemontcg.io: vintage = Paradijs scans (56/56), HGSS → today = malie (56/56).

sources.name: Limitless TCG
sources.origin: Japanese images mirror pokemon-card.com (so it has M6a 1–103 only, like the official site).

sources.name: Korean fan databases (collectory.cc, type-null/PTCG-database)
sources.origin: Every Korean site found hot-links pokemoncard.co.kr's watermarked images. None has a clean copy.

sources.name: tcg.mik.moe
sources.origin: Serves the WeChat app's images; nothing larger than the app's native size.

sources.name: Pokémon Central Wiki (it)

terms.summary: Text CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Images held as "fair use", each under its own file-page terms.

sources.origin: Modern: malie renders, stated on each file page ("Questa immagine proviene da malie.io"). Some 245×342 pokemon.com copies. Vintage: user uploads with no source; sets never printed in Italian use English scans with the Paradijs signature.

sources.name: WikiDex (es)

terms.summary: Text CC BY-SA 3.0. Images held as fair use, non-profit.

sources.origin: No source field. Modern files have the malie size. Vintage: user uploads, e.g. Base Set Charizard at 349×491 with a scanner resolution in its metadata. Below a 400 px floor for most uses.

sources.name: Bulbagarden Archives

terms.summary: Original content CC BY-NC-SA 2.5. Card images held as fair use.

sources.origin: One file per card, filed under every printing, so its "Japanese set" categories are largely English images. The Japanese secret rares are credited "From Pokeca.net" and carry pokeca.net's watermark.

examples.label: Phantump (Guardians Rising 6), filed under a JP set

sources.name: TCGdex

submissions.how: GitHub pull requests to cards-database (CONTRIBUTING rejects AI-assisted data PRs)

terms.summary: Card data MIT-licensed; the images aren't TCGdex's to license. Publishes no image credits.

sources.origin: By pixel match: HGSS → today in every Western language is ~100% malie. English 1999–2010 is 98–99% the Pokémon Paradijs scans. French vintage shares 50–73% of its files with pkmcards.fr. No German before HGSS. Its zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

stats.label: en+de (31,018 images)
stats.value: 76% malie · 15.5% Paradijs scans · 7% own HGSS/SM exports

sources.name: TCG Collector

submissions.how: Public "missing card images" contribution page; uploaders keep their rights

terms.summary: One copy for personal, transitory use. No mirroring. Uploaders keep their rights.

sources.origin: Credits "PkmnCards and Malie". Regular JP/ID cards: 84% official copies. English vintage: the Paradijs scans. Japanese vintage (1996–2006), SM/SwSh secret rares and McDonald's: its own users' scans (300 dpi, print texture). 19 secret-rare scans are identical to Bulbagarden's files.

examples.label: Rocket Gang Strikes Back (JP vintage, user scan)

stats.label: intl sample (533)
stats.value: 118 Paradijs scans; JP vintage own scans

sources.name: TCGplayer

api.note: Partner API; tcgcsv.com publishes a daily public dump of the catalogue

terms.summary: No public statement on catalogue images.

sources.origin: BW/XY/SM/HGSS/ME: malie renders. Neo, Platinum, EX Deoxys: the Paradijs scans (34/36). Base Set, Jungle, DP: its own small scans matching nothing else. SV Base: a clean digital export that isn't malie's.

sources.name: Cardmarket

terms.summary: No public statement on catalogue images. Site and image host block non-browser access.

sources.origin: Sampled via the Internet Archive (83 images). Modern cards: downscaled game renders. Vintage and prize-pack/staff stamps: its own scans. All too small to be useful.

sources.name: Serebii
sources.origin: Modern Japanese sets: pokemon-card.com's official images (30/30). English vintage: its own scans (600 dpi). BW/XY/SM: a digital export different from malie's.

sources.name: PriceCharting
sources.origin: Mostly photos and scans of physical cards: English vintage, Japanese VS/web, and Korean cards photographed in sleeves (glare, skew), so not a clean unwatermarked Korean source. Chinese Gem Pack: official images.

callouts.title: Korean: only watermarked images exist
callouts.body: Pokémon Korea's CDN serves only a watermarked directory (data/wmimages/…), and every Korean fan site hot-links those same files. PriceCharting's Korean images are photos of sleeved cards. No clean Korean card image was found anywhere, for any era (2010 → today).

callouts.title: Simplified Chinese: only the WeChat app, only 300×419
callouts.body: The only official source is Pokémon Shanghai's WeChat mini-program. Its images were scraped into the GitHub dataset duanxr/PTCG-CHS-Datasets at the app's native 300×419; nothing larger exists. The dataset forbids redistribution without Pokémon Shanghai's written consent. TCGdex's current zh-cn images are actually the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Better quality exists than TCGdex serves
callouts.body: TCGdex serves 600×825. malie's originals are 734×1024 with transparent corners; the Singapore English print on asia.pokemon-card.com is 744×1040; TCG Collector's Japanese scans reach 1280×1788; bisafans' German vintage photos are ≈ 860×1200.

callouts.title: Western 1999–2010 has no official digital image
callouts.body: TPC never put Base Set → Platinum in an online game or on pokemon.com. Every image of those cards, TCGdex's included, is somebody's scan. For English, nearly everyone uses the same Pokémon Paradijs scans.
